probes.query: Which Config method loads settings from environment variables that start with a given prefix?
expectedFacts: Config.from_prefixed_env loads env vars beginning with the prefix (default FLASK_), strips the prefix, and passes values through a loads function (default json.loads)
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '    def from_prefixed_env' src/flask/config.py -> config.py:126. Signature `def from_prefixed_env(self, prefix='FLASK', *, loads=json.loads) -> bool`.

probes.query: Find the helper that serializes its arguments to JSON and returns a Response with the application/json mimetype.
expectedFacts: jsonify is defined in src/flask/json/__init__.py and delegates to current_app.json.response() to build a Response with the application/json mimetype
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^def jsonify' src/flask/json/__init__.py -> json/__init__.py:138. Docstring states it calls app.json.response().

probes.query: How does Flask open the session for an incoming request and save it back into a Set-Cookie on the response? Trace from the default interface to where it is invoked.
expectedFacts: The default app.session_interface is SecureCookieSessionInterface (app.py:252); AppContext._get_session calls open_session (ctx.py:387-388) and finalize_request/process_response calls save_session (app.py:1416)
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^class SecureCookieSessionInterface\|    def open_session\|    def save_session' src/flask/sessions.py -> class@284, open_session@323, save_session@337. Wiring: grep -n 'session_interface' src/flask/app.py -> default @252, save_session call @1416; grep -n 'si.open_session' src/flask/ctx.py -> @388 (in _get_session @381).

probes.query: When a view calls flash(), where does the message get stored and how is it later retrieved for rendering? Also identify the signal that fires.
expectedFacts: flash appends (category, message) into the session under the '_flashes' key and sends the message_flashed signal; get_flashed_messages pops '_flashes' from the session (caching on app_ctx._flashes)
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^def flash\|^def get_flashed_messages' src/flask/helpers.py -> flash@326, get_flashed_messages@360. flash stores session['_flashes'] (helpers.py:349) and calls message_flashed.send (helpers.py:352). Signal: grep -n 'message_flashed = ' src/flask/signals.py -> signals.py:17.

probes.query: When app.register_blueprint(bp) is called, walk the chain that actually attaches the blueprint's view routes onto the application's URL map. Where does the per-rule endpoint prefixing and self.app.add_url_rule call happen? Don't get lost chasing nested blueprints or CLI command merging.
expectedFacts: register_blueprint calls Blueprint.register which builds a BlueprintSetupState and runs deferred functions; the rule prefixing and self.app.add_url_rule call live in BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule (sansio/blueprints.py:87)
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Rabbit-hole: register chain has tempting side-branches (_merge_blueprint_funcs, nested self._blueprints recursion, cli.commands merging) but the answer terminates at BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule. Verified: grep -n '    def register_blueprint' src/flask/sansio/app.py -> app.py:567 (calls blueprint.register). grep -n '    def register\b\|    def add_url_rule\|^class BlueprintSetupState' src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py -> BlueprintSetupState@34, BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule@87 (calls self.app.add_url_rule), Blueprint.register@273, Blueprint.add_url_rule@413.

probes.query: Where is the serializer that round-trips non-JSON-native types (UUID, datetime, bytes, tuples) for the session cookie, and what method reverses the tagging?
expectedFacts: TaggedJSONSerializer (json/tag.py:219) registers JSONTag subclasses and its untag method (json/tag.py:297) converts a tagged dict back into the original Python value
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^class TaggedJSONSerializer\|    def untag' src/flask/json/tag.py -> class@219, register@256, untag@297.

probes.query: When does Flask actually skip writing the session cookie, delete it, or add a 'Vary: Cookie' header? Point me at the method that decides this.
expectedFacts: SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session (sessions.py:337) adds 'Vary: Cookie' when the session was accessed, deletes the cookie when an empty session was modified, and otherwise relies on should_set_cookie before setting the signed cookie
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '    def save_session\|    def should_set_cookie' src/flask/sessions.py -> SessionInterface.should_set_cookie@233, SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session@337. save_session body @337-... contains response.vary.add('Cookie') and response.delete_cookie when empty+modified.

probes.query: How can a streaming/generator response keep access to request, session and g after the request context would normally have ended? Find the wrapper and how it preserves the context.
expectedFacts: stream_with_context (helpers.py) wraps a generator so it runs inside the current request context, keeping request, session and g available while the generator is consumed
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^def stream_with_context' src/flask/helpers.py -> three hits at 52, 58, 63 (two @overload stubs + the real impl at 63). Real impl docstring: 'Wrap a response generator function so that it runs inside the current request context. This keeps request, session, and g available'.

probes.query: Where does Flask implement request rate limiting / throttling (e.g. a token-bucket or leaky-bucket limiter)?
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified ABSENT: grep -rniE 'rate.?limit|throttl|leaky.?bucket|token.?bucket' src/flask/ -> 0 results (exit 1). Flask core has no rate limiting; it is provided by external extensions (e.g. Flask-Limiter).

probes.query: Which helper safely serves a file from within a directory using a client-supplied path?
expectedFacts: send_from_directory (helpers.py:543) serves a file from within a directory using werkzeug safe_join and delegates to send_file
probes.author: python-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^def send_from_directory' src/flask/helpers.py -> helpers.py:543. Docstring: 'Send a file from within a directory using send_file ... Uses werkzeug.security.safe_join'.
